messages:
sam.sells: Quick heads-up — Nighthawk POC kickoff this morning. They want to drop CompetitorX and route to Redwood. Main asks: prompt parity, how token billing maps to their old meter, SSO + KMS for private keys, and any known response deltas that affect downstream scoring. Can SRE/SEs weigh in?
omar.se: Thanks. Joining. Do they plan a drop-in proxy or an adapter shim?
sam.sells: They prefer a drop-in adapter to avoid changing customer prompts. They said ~200 TPS peak for 500ms latency target. Also worried about billing: CompetitorX billed per-request buckets, not tokens.
cara.engineering: We can do an adapter but two heads-up: (1) tokenization differences cause length deltas and billing mismatch, (2) incompatible default stop sequences can change outputs.
rebecca.solutions: On prompt parity we should run a small eval set — 150 prompts across their top flows (QA, summarization, classification). We can run A/B with CompetitorX and our recommended model + quantized variant.
derek.security: Security questions: they need KMS integration for customer keys, SCIM for provisioning, and an encrypted audit stream. Also they asked for a SOC2 addendum and data residency for EU customers.
sec-bot: @derek.security — submitted security questionnaire (link: https://security.redwood.example/nighthawk/480123). Attachment: questionnaire_v1.pdf
rebecca.solutions: Pricing — they asked how to approximate monthly cost when tokens vary. Suggested calc: convert their per-request buckets into average tokens per response from sampling then multiply by our per-token rate + embedding calls if they use similarity search.
omar.se: Practical mapping example for the adapter — competitor sends: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "summarize: ...",
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "stop": ["\n\n"]
}
```
We'll translate to Redwood's endpoint: 
```
POST /v1/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-large",
  "input": "summarize: ...",
  "max_output_tokens": 128,
  "stop_sequences": ["\n\n"]
}
```
Note: tokenizers differ, so output length may be +/− 5–10 tokens typically.
sam.sells: They also called out session state — CompetitorX preserves conversation state server-side with a session id. Can we offer an equivalent sticky-kv or should they just pass full convo?
cara.engineering: We support session pinning on Dedicated and Private deployments (pin to a worker with KV cache). For Hosted API, best practice is client-side context with our KV-cache header to reduce repeated tokens. We can provide a short-living session token for the POC.
derek.security: For KMS, we can support BYOK via our integration with AWS KMS and GCP KMS in Private. We'll need to add a small SA design doc and HSM notes for their compliance team.
rebecca.solutions: Acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Pass the 150-prompt parity suite with <= 2% major-regression rate; 2) Latency under 650ms P95 at their sample load; 3) Billing projection within 10% after sampling; 4) Security questionnaire signed + SCIM demo.
sam.sells: timeline? Nighthawk wants an internal demo in 10 business days.
omar.se: Plan: day 0–2 — onboarding + creds + security review; day 3–6 — implement adapter + smoke tests; day 7–9 — run parity suite & analyze; day 10 — demo. I'll spin up a small staging config.
rebecca.solutions: I'll prepare the eval harness and share a Colab + instructions. Also will include a quick script to estimate monthly spend from sample logs.
cara.engineering: Two engineering notes: (A) if they rely on exact stop token behavior for downstream parsers, we should add an output-normalization step in the adapter to reduce deltas, (B) watch for rare unicode tokenization edge-cases in product names — include in test set.
sam.sells: Perfect. @derek.security can you start the SA design doc and slot time with Nighthawk security? I'll ping legal for the SOC2 addendum.
derek.security: On it. Can we get their compliance contact + sample IP allowlist?
sam.sells: Sent (via DM).
rebecca.solutions: I'll post the parity harness link here when ready. Also tagging @omar.se for the adapter mapping PR once staging is up. :rocket:
omar.se: I'll create a quick proxy repo and share the smoke-run logs. Expect an initial PR by EOD tomorrow.
sam.sells: Awesome — thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the single source for the POC comms. :thumbsup:
